{"type": "item.completed", "item": {"id": "item_7", "type": "command_execution", "command": "/bin/bash -lc \"sed -n '1590,1660p' r
eference.md; sed -n '1739,1840p' reference.md; cat api-docs.md\"", "aggregated_output": "### `cloud eval run`\n\nStart an eval run
of an existing suite, or upload a versioned suite file and run it. Provide **either** `--suite` **or** `--file`, not both.\n\nBy
default the command prints a launch receipt and returns immediately. `--wait` polls every launched run to a terminal state.\n\n**E
xit codes (`--wait` only).** Without `--wait` this command's exit code is unchanged: `0` on any launch, `1` on a partial or wholly
failed fan-out. `--wait` owns a separate six-code contract — a caller who asked this process to sit and watch a run to completion

is asking it to say how the run went:

| Code | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `0` | Every waited run passed, unanimously, and (when a
report was requested) every report was assembled |\n| `1` | A run **completed** with a **failed** verdict. The only condition tha
t produces this code |\n| `2` | Usage error — bad flags, `--reporter`/`--out` without `--wait`, or an invalid suite file (after au
th, before any server/model work) |\n| `3` | Auth failed — no credential, or the platform rejected it, at launch or mid-wait (a to
ken that expired during a long poll). Zero credits spent if it happened before launch |\n| `4` | Connection/setup failed before ev
aluation — a launch failure this CLI itself observed (network, timeout, rate limit, a partial or failed fan-out, an unrecognized l
aunch error), or a local `--out` write failure — unless a more severe outcome (`1` or `3`) already applies to the same run, per th
e merge order above |\n| `5` | No valid verdict — `inconclusive`, a null/unrecognized result, a run whose own status is failed/can
celled/timed-out, a wait that hit its deadline, a mid-wait failure that was not auth-shaped, or a report that could not be assembl
ed |\n\nNo infrastructure condition ever maps to `1` — see the same rule under `eval gate` below. A multi-target launch merges the
se worst-of across every waited run, in the order `1 > 3 > 4 > 5 > 0`: a real verdict failure is never masked by a sibling's infra
structure noise, and a credential failure (which may be *why* other targets show no verdict) outranks a plain connection failure.\
n\nThis six-code contract is new and deliberately **different** from `eval gate`'s four codes below — see that command's own doc f
or why the two are not unified. An invalid suite file exits **2** either way — `eval validate` still exits 1 for the same contract

failure, because it is a verdict on the file and this command is not.

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--s
uite <id-or-name>` | Yes, unless `--file` | Eval suite name or ID |\n| `--file <path>` | Yes, unless `--suite` | Versioned suite f
ile to upload and run (`.yaml` or `.json`, or `-` for stdin) |\n| `--project <id-or-name>` | No | Project name or ID (defaults to
the most recently updated project) |\n| `--server <id-or-name...>` | No | Override the suite's saved server selection (HTTP server
s only) |\n| `--environment <id-or-name...>` | No | Attached project environment(s) to run. Several values start one **paid run ea
ch**. |\n| `--client <id-or-name...>` | No | Attached client(s) to run, so the run is stamped with that client's config. Several v
alues start one **paid run each**. |\n| `--host <id-or-name...>` | No | **Deprecated** alias for `--client`. Passing both is an er
ror. Not the host-compat catalog id `mcpjam compat --host` / `mcpjam tools --host` take — see [Two different `--host` flags](#two-
different---host-flags). |\n| `--all-targets` | No | Run **every** attached environment (or, if none, every attached host) — one *
*paid run per target** |\n| `--iterations <n>` | No | Run each case this many times (1-10), for this run only |\n| `--repetitions
<n>` | No | **Legacy** spelling of `--iterations`. Passing both is an error. |\n| `--case <id-or-title...>` | No | Run only these
cases instead of the whole suite |\n| `--exclude-skills` | No | Run the \"without skills\" A/B arm: nothing is pinned, and the run
is labelled as excluded |\n| `--refresh-snapshot` | No | **Persists a new host-config snapshot on the suite** (see below). Single
-target runs only. |\n| `--notes <text>` | No | Free-text note stored on the run |\n| `--min-pass-rate <n>` | No | Pass threshold
for this run (0-100), overriding the suite's own |\n| `--match-options <json>` | No | Tool-call match options for this run, e.g. `
'{\"toolCallOrder\":\"exact\"}'` |\n| `--idempotency-key <key>` | No | Retry key for a lost launch response. For `--file`, a fresh
key is minted and printed on every invocation when this flag is omitted; supply the printed key to replay the same run instead of
starting a new one |\n| `--wait` | No | Wait for every launched run to reach a terminal status |\n| `--wait-timeout <ms>` | No |
Maximum wait time (default 2100000); requires `--wait` |\n| `--reporter <json-summary\\|junit-xml\\|html>` | No | Write the comple
ted structured report to stdout; requires `--wait`. `html` is a self-contained decision summary + failures page — traces/parity/hi
story are not included. |\n| `--out <path>` | No | Atomically write the completed report to a file; defaults to `json-summary`, or
uses `--reporter` when present; requires `--wait` |\n| `--compose-client <id-or-name>` | No | Compose a stack to run instead of n
aming a saved environment (see below). **Ephemeral by default** — pass `--save-targets` to attach it to the suite. |\n| `--compose
-host <id-or-name>` | No | **Deprecated** alias for `--compose-client` |\n| `--compose-computer <id-or-name>` | No | Sandbox image
to pin on the composed stack |\n| `--compose-model <id...>` | No | Model(s) to run on the composed stack. Replaces the client's p
inned model unless `--with-client-default` is set |\n| `--compose-model-selection <json...>` | No | Whole saved model selection(s)
— source, connection, `settings.reasoningEffort` — as JSON: one cell per selection, for its model, at its effort. Repeat to add s
everal selections for one model (e.g. at low and at high) — each distinct selection is its own cell |\n| `--with-client-default` |
No | Also launch an inherit cell using each client's pinned model, alongside `--compose-model` |\n| `--compose-server <id-or-name
...>` | No | Server(s) to pin on the composed stack, snapshotted into a server group so a rerun keeps testing them. Mutually exclu
sive with `--compose-server-group` |\n| `--compose-server-group <id>` | No | Standalone server group to pin on the composed stack
|\n| `--compose-host-servers` | No | **No longer supported** — rejected. An eval run takes its servers from a server group alone;
use `--compose-server` or `--compose-server-group` |\n| `--compose-skill <id...>` | No | Project-shared skill IDs to pin on the co
mposed stack |\n| `--compose-secret <id...>` | No | Project secret IDs the composed stack grants to its runs (`secrets list` shows
them) |\n| `--save-targets` | No | Attach the composed environments to the suite (append, capped at 10). Without it the stack is

ephemeral |

#### Composing a target instead of naming one

`--compose-client <id-or-name>` builds an execution stack for this
run instead of\nnaming a saved environment, refined by `--compose-computer`, `--compose-model`,\n`--compose-server-group`, `--com
pose-skill` and `--compose-secret`. The stack becomes an unnamed,\ncontent-addressed environment (the same one `environments ensur
e-adhoc`\nproduces), so composing the same stack twice reuses one environment.\n`--compose-host` is the deprecated spelling of the

same flag.

`--compose-model` and `--compose-secret` carry the deployment requirement
described under [Deployment support for
model overrides and secret\ngrants](#deployment-support-for-model-overrides-and-secret-grants): a launch that names\neither is ref
used before it composes anything if this deployment does not\npublish the capability.\n#### `--file`: upload and run a suite file\
n\n`eval run --file` reads the versioned suite file (`schemaVersion: \"1\"`),\nauthenticates, then validates. A contract-invalid f
ile exits **2** after the\nauth request — it does not start a run. `eval validate` on the same bytes\nstill exits 1: that command

is a verdict on the file; this one is not.

The file's `suite.id` is the declared suite identity. The first run creates a
